docs.title: CLI Shortcuts & Hotkeys
docs.text: YAICLI offers a rich set of keyboard shortcuts and interactive features to enhance your command-line experience. This page covers all available shortcuts and interactive functionalities.

docs.title: Global Shortcuts
docs.text:
These shortcuts work in all interactive modes:

Shortcut Description Ctrl+C Clear the current input line (during generation: cancel the turn); press twice quickly to exit Ctrl+D Exit the application Shift+Tab Toggle between Chat/Execute modes Ctrl+R Search command history Ctrl+O Open the full-screen tool-output viewer for this turn (↑/↓ select, Tab switch pane, f full text, q/Esc close). Also works while the assistant is generating: generation continues in the background and closing the viewer redraws the accumulated answer ↑/↓ Navigate through command history Alt+Enter (Esc, Enter) Insert a newline instead of submitting the prompt Ctrl+J Insert a newline (same as Alt+Enter); Enter still submits the whole input / Open the slash-command completion menu (all commands with descriptions; /co filters; Tab/arrows select) Ctrl+L Clear the screen Ctrl+A Move cursor to beginning of line Ctrl+E Move cursor to end of line Ctrl+U Clear charactors before cursor Ctrl+W Delete word before cursor

docs.title: History Navigation
docs.text:
When searching history with Ctrl+R:

Shortcut Description Ctrl+R Cycle through matching history items Enter Select current history item Esc Cancel history search

docs.title: Interactive Commands
docs.text:
YAICLI provides special commands that begin with a slash (/) or an exclamation mark (!):

Command Description /help or /? Show help message /clear Clear the current conversation history /his Show chat history /list List all saved chat sessions /save <title> Save the current chat session with a title /load <index> Load a saved chat session /del <index> Delete a saved chat session /exit Exit the application /mode chat\|exec Switch between chat and execute modes /cost Show session token usage and estimated cost /compact [keep_rounds] Compact the conversation, keeping the last N turn groups /model [name] Show or switch the model for this session /role [name] Show or switch the assistant role /retry Re-run the last user turn from its pre-turn snapshot !<command> Execute a shell command directly

With !<command>, you can execute a shell command directly without leaving the interactive mode. For example, !ls -al will list files in the current directory, !git status will show the git status, etc.

docs.title: Chat Sessions & Resume
docs.text:
Chat sessions are saved per working directory in ~/.yaicli/sessions/ since v0.21; see Chat Sessions & Resume for the store layout, metadata and migration of old sessions.

Command Behaviour ai --chat Start a temporary interactive session ai --chat "<title>" Continue the session with that title in the current project. A missing title prints an explicit notice and starts a new persistent session with that title (never a silent fallback) ai --resume Continue the newest saved session of the current project (implies --chat). With no saved session it prints an explicit notice and starts a new temporary session ai --list-chats List saved sessions of the invocation directory (the callback runs before --cwd applies)

--resume is interactive only: combined with -p/--print or a non-text --output-format it is ignored with a warning and the run continues one-shot; the same happens when stdin is redirected. It takes no title — use --chat "<title>" to load a specific session. Run ai from the project directory (or use --cwd) so the per-project store matches the session you want.

docs.title: Auto-Suggestion
docs.text:
YAICLI offers auto-suggestions based on your command history. As you type, it shows light gray text suggesting completions from your history:

  • Press → (right arrow) to accept the full suggestion
  • Continue typing to ignore the suggestion
  • Press Esc then f to accept one word of the suggestion

To disable auto-suggestions, set AUTO_SUGGEST=false in your configuration.

docs.title: Multi-line and Long Input
docs.text:
The prompt supports multiline editing: press Alt+Enter (or Esc then Enter) or Ctrl+J to insert a newline, and Enter alone to submit the whole buffer. This is handy for pasting logs or composing long instructions. The prompt itself is just the mode icon and >, so the cursor position never changes; the current model and last-known context usage appear on the dim status line after each answer (see Interactive Mode).

For long or multi-line prompts in scripts, pass the text as a quoted argument or pipe it:

# Quote a multi-line string
ai "$(cat prompt.txt)"

# Pipe content and add an instruction
cat error.log | ai "Explain these errors"

# Here-document
ai "$(cat <<'EOF'
Summarize the following log and list the root cause:
<paste log here>
EOF
)"

Piped stdin is combined with the prompt argument (stdin content comes first).

docs.title: Command Editing
docs.text:
When in Execute mode and reviewing a suggested command:

Option Description e Edit the command before execution y Execute the command as is n Cancel execution

When editing a command:

  • The full command is presented in an editable field
  • Make your changes and press Enter to execute
  • Press Esc to cancel the edit

docs.title: Visual Indicators
docs.text:
YAICLI uses visual indicators to help you understand the current state:

Indicator Meaning 💬 > Chat mode prompt 🚀 > Execute mode prompt Cursor animation Processing your request Syntax highlighting Code in responses

docs.title: Input Methods
docs.text: YAICLI accepts input through various methods:

docs.title: Direct Input
docs.text: ai "What is the capital of France?"

docs.title: Piped Input
docs.text: echo "What is the capital of France?" | ai

docs.title: File Analysis
docs.text: cat error.log | ai "Explain these errors"

docs.title: Combined Input
docs.text: cat data.csv | ai "Convert this CSV to JSON"

docs.title: Image Input
docs.text:
# Local image file
ai --image photo.jpg "What is in this image?"

# Multiple images
ai -i img1.png -i img2.png "Compare these"

# Image URL
ai --image https://example.com/photo.jpg "Describe this"

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text:
YAICLI returns a non-zero exit status for failures it can detect, so scripts and CI can tell success from failure:

Exit code Meaning 0 Success (answer produced; informational commands such as --version, --list-*). 1 A handled failure: invalid/malformed configuration, unknown or misconfigured provider, missing/invalid API key or API error, retry exhaustion, no input/aborted action, or an unexpected error printed as Unknown error: .... 2 Usage error: an invalid option or argument. 3 A tool call was denied and --fail-on-tool-denied was set. 130 Interrupted by SIGINT (Ctrl+C) during a one-shot run or generation. 141 Broken pipe (EPIPE); ai --help \| head -1 is safe and exits 0/141.

A failure report such as Unknown error: API_KEY is required is accompanied by exit code 1; if you see a failure message with exit code 0, that is a bug. Verify the current build with:

ai --version; echo "exit=$?"

Inside the interactive --chat REPL, an error during one turn is printed and the session continues; the process exits 0 when you leave the REPL normally. Use single-shot mode (-p or a prompt argument) when you need the exit code to reflect the request outcome. The full scripting contract (JSON output, signals, non-interactive approvals) is in Headless & Scripting.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Learn about different interaction modes
  • Explore configuration options
  • Check out command references

docs.title: Command Reference
docs.text: YAICLI provides a versatile command-line interface with multiple options and modes. This page covers all available commands and options.

docs.title: Basic Syntax
docs.text:
ai [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]

Where PROMPT is the text input for the agent. If not provided, YAICLI reads from stdin when it is piped; with no prompt and no stdin it starts the interactive REPL. Use -p/--print to force a single one-shot run, and see Headless & Scripting for the full scripting contract.

docs.title: Command Line Reference
docs.text: Here's a comprehensive list of all available options:

docs.title: Core Options
docs.text: Option Short Description --help -h Show help message and exit --verbose -V Show verbose output (loaded config, API calls, etc.) --version -v Show version and exit (fast path; does not read config) --template Show the default config file template and exit --list-providers List available providers and exit

docs.title: Headless / Scripting Options
docs.text:
Option Short Description --print -p Explicit one-shot mode: run once, never start the REPL --output-format text\|json\|stream-json Output format for the result (default text; stream-json is NDJSON events) --json Shorthand for --output-format json --quiet -q Only print the answer to stdout (no labels/progress) --max-turns N Maximum tool-call rounds for this run (overrides MAX_TOOL_CALL_DEPTH) --yes -y Auto-approve read-level tools only; write/exec tools still need a rule --allowed-tools "a,b*" Per-run tool allowlist, comma-separated names or globs --cwd DIR Working directory / workspace root for the run (also selects the project for sessions and project context) --fail-on-tool-denied Exit with code 3 when a tool was denied

See Headless & Scripting for JSON schemas, exit codes and signal handling, and Permissions & Safety for --yes / --allowed-tools semantics.

docs.title: Mode Options
docs.text: Option Short Description --chat -c Start in interactive chat mode --shell -s Generate and optionally execute shell commands (in a non-TTY: print only) --code Generate code in plaintext --print -p Explicit one-shot mode (see above)

docs.title: LLM Options
docs.text: Option Short Description Default --model -M Specify the model to use Configured default --temperature -T Set temperature (randomness) 0.3 --top-p -P Set top-p sampling 1.0 --max-tokens Set max tokens in response 1024 --stream / --no-stream Enable/disable streaming stream

docs.title: Role Options
docs.text: Option Short Description --role -r Specify the assistant role to use --create-role Create a new role with the specified name --delete-role Delete a role with the specified name --list-roles List all available roles --show-role Show the role with the specified name

docs.title: Chat Options
docs.text:
Option Description --resume Continue the most recent saved session of the current project (implies --chat; interactive only) --list-chats List saved chat sessions of the invocation directory (runs before --cwd applies)

See Chat Sessions & Resume for the per-project store, --resume details and the --list-chats caveat.

docs.title: Display Options
docs.text: Option Short Description Default --justify -j Text alignment (default, left, center, right, full) default --show-reasoning / --hide-reasoning Show/hide reasoning content show

docs.title: Function Options
docs.text:
Option Description Default --install-functions Export editable copies of the built-in functions into the config dir (built-ins work without this; existing files are skipped) --reinstall-functions Overwrite exported built-in copies with the current version; custom files are kept --list-functions List loaded tools, their source (builtin/user) and stale-copy warnings --enable-functions / --disable-functions Enable/disable function calling in API requests enabled --show-function-output / --hide-function-output Show/hide function output show --tools Comma-separated tool-name globs to offer the model (fnmatch; MCP tools use the _mcp__ prefix). Empty = all tools. Shrinks the per-request schema payload, e.g. --tools 'fs_*,web_search' all tools

Selecting a subset is also possible persistently with ENABLED_TOOLS in config.ini / YAI_ENABLED_TOOLS (see Configuration). A tool that is not offered is also refused if the model calls it anyway, with an in-band error the model can read.

See Advanced Usage — Function Calling for custom functions, updating after an upgrade, and built-in safety contracts. See Permissions & Safety for the confirmation protocol, rules and audit log.

docs.title: MCP Options
docs.text: Option Description Default --enable-mcp / --disable-mcp Enable/disable MCP in API requests disabled --show-mcp-output / --hide-mcp-output Show/hide MCP output hide --list-mcp List all available MCP

docs.title: Image Options
docs.text: Option Short Description --image -i Image file path or URL to include with the prompt. Can be specified multiple times.

docs.title: Common Command Examples
docs.text:
# Agent task: let the model pick and run tools
ai "Use your tools to find the 3 largest files here and write a summary to REPORT.md"

# One-shot with machine-readable output
ai -p "summarize the git log" --output-format json

# Answer-only output (for pipelines)
ai -q -p "list the open TODOs in src/"

# Get a quick answer
ai "What is the capital of France?"

# Start an interactive chat session
ai --chat

# Save chat with a title
ai --chat "Python programming tips"

# Continue the newest saved session of this project
ai --resume

# Generate and execute shell commands
ai --shell "Create a backup of my Documents folder"

# Generate code snippets (Python by default)
ai --code "Write a function to sort a list"

# Use a specific LLM model
ai --model gpt-4-turbo "Explain quantum computing"

# Adjust temperature for more creative responses
ai --temperature 0.8 "Write a poem about AI"

# Create a custom role
ai --create-role "SQL Expert"

# Use a custom role
ai --role "SQL Expert" "Optimize this query"

# Show verbose output for debugging
ai --verbose "Test query"

# Send an image to a vision model
ai --image photo.jpg "What is in this image?"

# Send multiple images for comparison
ai -i img1.png -i img2.png "Compare these screenshots"

# Send an image URL
ai --image https://example.com/photo.jpg "Describe this"

# Image-only (no text prompt)
ai --image diagram.png

docs.title: Interactive Mode Commands
docs.text:
When in interactive chat or shell mode, you can use these special commands:

Command Description /help or /? Show help message /clear Clear conversation history /his Show chat history /list List saved chats /save <title> Save current chat with title /load <index> Load a saved chat /del <index> Delete a saved chat /exit Exit the application /mode chat\|exec Switch between chat and execute modes /add <path> Add file or directory to context /context or /ctx Show estimated context/token usage for the current conversation /context <subcmd> Manage file context (list, add, remove, clear) /compact [keep_rounds] Compact the conversation, keeping the last N turns /permissions List session approvals, the persistent allowlist and the numbered rules /permissions revoke <tool-or-index> Remove a persistent permission by tool name or rule number (the tool will ask again) /show-output Open the full-screen viewer listing every tool output of the current turn (same as Ctrl+O) /undo Restore the last file change made by a guarded tool in this session (see Workspace Safety) /cost Show session token usage, estimated cost, per-model breakdown and tool metrics /model Show the current model and provider /model <name> Switch the model for this session; the provider client is rebuilt on the next request, the chat history is kept, and the notice names the previous model so it can be reverted /role Show the current role and the available roles /role <name> Switch the assistant role for this session (case-insensitive; unknown names list the available roles) /retry Re-run the last user turn from its pre-turn snapshot (useful after an API error; partial messages from the failed turn are discarded)

docs.title: Context Management Commands
docs.text:
The /add and /context commands help you manage files and directories in the conversation context:

Command Description /add <path> Add a file or directory to the persistent context /context list or /ctx list List all items in current context /context clear or /ctx clear Remove all items from context /context add <path> Add item to context (same as /add) /context remove <path> or /ctx remove <path> Remove specific item from context

Context Features:

  • Persistent: Items added with /add stay in context for the entire session
  • Smart reading: Files are read and formatted for AI consumption
  • Directory support: Directories are scanned recursively (2 levels deep by default)
  • Auto-ignores: Skips .git, node_modules, __pycache__, .venv, etc.
  • Flexible matching: Use partial paths or filenames for removal

Example:

💬 > /add src/main.py
Added file to context: /path/to/src/main.py

💬 > /add tests/
Added directory to context: /path/to/tests/

💬 > /context list
┏━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ Type   ┃ Path                          ┃
┡━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ FILE   │ src/main.py                   │
│ DIR    │ tests/                        │
└────────┴───────────────────────────────┘

💬 > /context remove main.py
Removed from context: /path/to/src/main.py

💬 > /ctx clear
Context cleared.

docs.title: @ File References
docs.text:
In addition to persistent context, you can temporarily reference files using the @ symbol directly in your queries:

Syntax:

# Single file reference
@filename

# Multiple files
@file1.py @file2.py

# Paths with spaces (use quotes)
@"my document.txt"
@'path with spaces/file.md'

How it works:

  1. Type @ followed by a file path
  2. Press Tab for auto-completion and file browser
  3. Use arrow keys to select files
  4. The file content is automatically included in that message only
  5. References are replaced with filenames in the final message

Example:

# Quick file analysis
💬 > @README.md Summarize this project

# Compare files
💬 > @config.json @config.example.json What changed?

# Use with quotes for spaces
💬 > @"my notes.txt" Create a todo list from these notes

# Path completion
💬 > @src/ma[Tab]
# Shows: src/main.py, src/math.py, etc.

Differences from /add:

Feature /add @ reference Duration Entire session Single message only Storage Persistent context Temporary inclusion Best for Codebases you'll discuss repeatedly Quick one-time file checks Management Manual add/remove Automatic per message

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Description Shift+Tab Toggle between Chat/Execute modes Ctrl+C Clear the current input line; during generation it cancels the turn; press twice quickly to exit Ctrl+D Exit (exit code 0) Ctrl+R Search history Ctrl+O Open the full-screen tool-output viewer for this turn (q/Esc to close); works during generation too (generation continues in the background; closing redraws the accumulated answer) ↑/↓ Navigate through history Alt+Enter (or Esc, Enter) Insert a newline instead of submitting Ctrl+J Insert a newline (same as Alt+Enter); Enter still submits / Open the slash-command completion menu (every command plus a one-line description; /co filters)

docs.title: Configuration Guide
docs.text: YAICLI uses a layered configuration system to store your preferences and API keys. This guide explains all available configuration options and how to customize them.

docs.title: Configuration Hierarchy
docs.text:
YAICLI follows this priority order for configuration:

  1. Command-line arguments (highest priority)
  2. Environment variables
  3. Configuration file
  4. Default values (lowest priority)

docs.title: Location
docs.text:
YAICLI resolves its configuration directory in this order:

  1. YAI_CONFIG_DIR (explicit override)
  2. XDG_CONFIG_HOME/yaicli
  3. %APPDATA%/yaicli on Windows
  4. ~/.config/yaicli (fallback, e.g. Linux/macOS without XDG set)

The configuration file is config.ini inside that directory. It may contain an API key, so it is created with mode 0600 (and the directory with 0700). On a read-only HOME or container, YAICLI keeps working with defaults and only warns once when it cannot persist state.

The prompt history file follows XDG state conventions: $XDG_STATE_HOME/yaicli/history when XDG_STATE_HOME is set, otherwise ~/.yaicli_history.

docs.title: First-time Setup
docs.text:
1. Run a real model command once (e.g. ai "hi"); the default configuration file is created on first use
  2. Edit the file to add your API key and customize settings (or export YAI_API_KEY instead)

--version and --help never write state, so they are safe in read-only environments.

docs.title: Viewing Default Configuration
docs.text:
To view the default configuration template:

ai --template

docs.title: Configuration File Structure
docs.text:
The configuration file uses the INI format with the following sections:

[core]
PROVIDER=openai
BASE_URL=
API_KEY=
MODEL=gpt-5.2

DEFAULT_ROLE=DEFAULT
# auto detect shell and os (or specify manually, e.g., bash, zsh, powershell.exe)
SHELL_NAME=auto
OS_NAME=auto

# true: streaming response, false: non-streaming
STREAM=true

# LLM parameters
TEMPERATURE=0.3
FREQUENCY_PENALTY=0.0
TOP_P=1.0
MAX_TOKENS=1024
TIMEOUT=60
# JSON strings
EXTRA_HEADERS=
EXTRA_BODY=
REASONING_EFFORT=

# Interactive mode parameters
INTERACTIVE_ROUND=25

# UI/UX
CODE_THEME=monokai
# Max entries kept in history file
MAX_HISTORY=500
AUTO_SUGGEST=true
# Print reasoning content or not
SHOW_REASONING=true
# Text alignment (default, left, center, right, full)
JUSTIFY=default

# Chat history settings (v0.21 K13: sessions are per project by default)
# Explicit override: keep the old flat directory. Leave/remove the line (or keep the
# built-in default value) to use ~/.yaicli/sessions/<hash of the working directory>/.
# CHAT_HISTORY_DIR=/home/me/yaicli-sessions
MAX_SAVED_CHATS=20

# Role settings
# Set to false to disable warnings about modified built-in roles
ROLE_MODIFY_WARNING=true

# Function settings
# Set to false to disable sending functions in API requests
ENABLE_FUNCTIONS=true
# Set to false to disable showing function output in the response
SHOW_FUNCTION_OUTPUT=true
# Comma-separated tool-name globs to offer the model (empty = all tools).
# Builtin and MCP tools are both matched; MCP names carry the _mcp__ prefix.
ENABLED_TOOLS=

# MCP settings
ENABLE_MCP=false
SHOW_MCP_OUTPUT=false
# Seconds one MCP list/call operation may take (0 = no timeout)
MCP_TIMEOUT=30
# Max MCP tools offered to the model per request (0 = unlimited)
MCP_MAX_TOOLS=64

# Observability & cost (v0.22)
# Print one token/cost line after each interactive turn
SHOW_USAGE=true
# json string overriding the built-in price table, e.g.
# {"gpt-4o": {"input": 2.5, "output": 10}}  (USD per 1M tokens)
MODEL_PRICING=

# Provider-specific settings
# MiniMax: request reasoning content separately (interleaved thinking); ignored by others
MINIMAX_REASONING_SPLIT=true
# Anthropic: true = one tool call per response (compatibility default); false = allow parallel calls
DISABLE_PARALLEL_TOOL_USE=true

# Tool confirmation (set to false to restore silent execution)
TOOL_CONFIRM=true

# Session-wide tool permission mode (v0.21): readonly | standard | trusted
# readonly: auto-allow read/network tools only; write/exec tools are always denied
# standard: ask for confirmation / use tool_permissions.json rules (default)
# trusted: auto-allow every non-dangerous tool (dangerous shell commands still ask)
TOOL_POLICY=standard

# Maximum recursive tool-call rounds per request
MAX_TOOL_CALL_DEPTH=8

# Comma-separated API parameters to omit from requests, e.g. temperature,top_p
EXCLUDE_PARAMS=

# Agent context settings (v0.19)
# Max characters of one tool result kept in the context (0 = no truncation);
# the full output is saved to TOOL_OUTPUT_DIR.
TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS=32000
# Scratch directory for full (untruncated) tool outputs; independent of the
# per-project session store. Defaults to <tempdir>/yaicli/chats/tool-outputs.
TOOL_OUTPUT_DIR=<tempdir>/yaicli/chats/tool-outputs
# Redact known secret shapes (API keys, tokens, private keys, ...) before tool
# output and saved sessions are written to disk. The model still sees the real
# content; only the on-disk copies are sanitized.
REDACT_SECRETS=true
# Terminal display of tool results (v0.19.1): head-only preview; the model still
# receives TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS. 0 = show everything.
TOOL_DISPLAY_MAX_LINES=15
TOOL_DISPLAY_MAX_CHARS=4000
# Max characters of the "@Function call:" argument line (0 = raw arguments).
TOOL_CALL_PREVIEW_MAX_CHARS=300
# Token budget for one request; 0 = derive from the model context window
# (window - MAX_TOKENS - CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS). Set explicitly to override.
CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS=0
# Model context windows (JSON): "model" / "provider:model" / "provider/model"
# keys; values are token counts or {"window": N, "max_output": M}.
# Empty = resolve via learned/metadata/catalog/heuristic layers.
MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS={}
# Probe provider metadata (OpenRouter / Gemini / Ollama) for the model window.
ENABLE_MODEL_METADATA=true
# Safety headroom kept below (window - MAX_TOKENS) when deriving the request budget.
CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS=1024
# Cache resolved windows under <config-dir>/cache/model_limits.json.
ENABLE_MODEL_LIMITS_CACHE=true

# Project context settings (v0.21 K12)
# Auto-load .yaicli.md / AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md from the working directory up to the
# git root and add them to the system prompt. false = no project-file reads at all.
ENABLE_PROJECT_CONTEXT=true
# Max characters of project instructions added to the system prompt
# (0 = no cap; a truncated block prints one warning naming the files involved).
PROJECT_CONTEXT_MAX_CHARS=20000

# Shell tool settings (v0.19)
# Max seconds a shell command may run (killed with its process group on timeout).
TOOL_TIMEOUT=120
# true = pass the full parent environment to shell commands (old behaviour);
# false = filtered environment, secrets such as YAI_API_KEY are not passed.
TOOL_ENV_INHERIT=false
# Workspace root for shell cwd and guarded file writes (empty = current directory).
WORKSPACE_ROOT=

# Reliability settings (v0.19)
RETRY_ENABLED=true
RETRY_MAX=2
RETRY_BASE_DELAY=1.0
# Maximum delay between retries in seconds (caps the exponential backoff)
RETRY_MAX_DELAY=8.0
# Exit non-zero in one-shot mode when the tool-call depth limit is reached.
EXIT_ON_DEPTH_LIMIT=true

# Tool audit log (v0.19)
# Write one JSON line per tool decision to tool_audit.jsonl in the config dir.
TOOL_AUDIT=true

Comments in config.ini must be on their own line. Inline comments are not stripped by the INI parser and become part of the value (e.g. PROVIDER=openai # note would make the provider name invalid).

docs.title: Context Management
docs.text:
Conversation context is bounded on three levels; see Context & Limits for the full behaviour:

  • Per-tool truncation: TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS (default 32000 chars) keeps head/tail and spills the full output to TOOL_OUTPUT_DIR.
  • Token budget: CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS (default 0 = derive from the resolved model window as window - MAX_TOKENS - CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS; > 0 = verbatim override) is enforced before each request; over-budget history is trimmed by turn group, keeping assistant tool_calls and their tool results together. The window itself comes from MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS, provider metadata, the bundled catalog or a family heuristic — see Context & Limits.
  • REPL retention: INTERACTIVE_ROUND (default 25) is the number of chat turns kept in the REPL (×2 messages), not a token limit. MAX_HISTORY (default 500) only sizes the prompt history file (see Conversation & History).
  • Project instructions: .yaicli.md / AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md are auto-loaded into the system prompt (ENABLE_PROJECT_CONTEXT, PROJECT_CONTEXT_MAX_CHARS; see Project Context).

Use /context to inspect the estimated usage and /compact [keep_rounds] to compact manually (see Command Reference).

docs.title: Chat Sessions
docs.text:
Since v0.21, chat sessions are isolated per project. With the default configuration CHAT_HISTORY_DIR is unset, and sessions are stored in ~/.yaicli/sessions/<sha256(resolved cwd)[:16]>/ (directories 0700, session files 0600). Setting an explicit CHAT_HISTORY_DIR that differs from the built-in default (<tempdir>/yaicli/chats) restores the old flat directory for all projects; a value equal to the built-in default counts as unset. MAX_SAVED_CHATS applies within the active store.

Each saved session records model, provider, role, cwd, created_at and updated_at in its JSON, so a resumed session describes how it was produced. Sessions saved by older versions load normally and are backfilled on their next save. Use --resume to continue the newest session of the current project — see Chat Sessions & Resume.

docs.title: State Files
docs.text: Path Purpose <config-dir>/config.ini Main configuration (mode 0600) <config-dir>/roles/ Role definitions <config-dir>/functions/ User/exported function definitions <config-dir>/functions_manifest.json Version/hash manifest for stale copied-function detection <config-dir>/mcp.json MCP server configuration <config-dir>/tool_permissions.json Persistent tool allow rules (mode 0600) <config-dir>/tool_audit.jsonl Tool decision audit log <tempdir>/yaicli/chats/tool-outputs/ Spilled full tool outputs (legacy scratch dir; TOOL_OUTPUT_DIR overrides) ~/.yaicli/sessions/<hash>/ Saved chat sessions per project, mode 0700 dirs / 0600 files (or an explicit CHAT_HISTORY_DIR) $XDG_STATE_HOME/yaicli/history or ~/.yaicli_history REPL prompt history (mode 0600)

docs.title: Syntax Highlighting Themes
docs.text:
YAICLI supports all Pygments syntax highlighting themes. Set your preferred theme with:

CODE_THEME = monokai

Browse available themes at: https://pygments.org/styles/

docs.title: Extra Headers and Body
docs.text:
You can add extra headers and body parameters to the API request:

EXTRA_HEADERS={"X-Extra-Header": "value"}
EXTRA_BODY={"extra_key": "extra_value"}

Example: Disable Qwen3's thinking behavior:

EXTRA_BODY={"enable_thinking": false}

Or limit thinking tokens:

EXTRA_BODY={"thinking_budget": 4096}

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Every option in the reference table above can be set with its YAI_* environment variable (these override the config file):

# Set API key via environment variable
export YAI_API_KEY="your-api-key"

# Use a different model
export YAI_MODEL="gpt-3.5-turbo"

# Disable streaming
export YAI_STREAM="false"

Environment variables take precedence over the configuration file settings.

Provider-specific keys that are not in the table (for example HF_PROVIDER, AZURE_ENDPOINT, AWS_*, AK/SK) are read by the individual provider implementations from the config file or their usual environment variables; they do not have a YAI_ alias.

docs.title: Provider-Specific Configuration
docs.text: See the Providers section for detailed configuration options for each supported LLM provider.

docs.title: Context & Limits
docs.text: Long agent tasks have a failure mode that chat tools do not: a single tool result (a log file, a directory listing, a web page) can be larger than the model's context window. YAICLI bounds this on three levels — per-tool truncation, a per-request token budget, and turn-group-aligned history trimming — and heals a context-length rejection instead of failing permanently.

docs.title: 1. Tool-output truncation
docs.text:
Every tool result is truncated before it enters the conversation:

  • only the head and tail of the output are kept, with a marker in the middle;
  • the full output is written to disk so nothing is lost;
  • the marker tells the model where the full text is and how to page through it.

The default cap is TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS=32000 characters (≈8k tokens). Built-in tools have per-tool caps on top of the global default:

Tool Approx. cap fs_read_file 64 KB fetch_webpage (body) 100 KB fs_search_files, fs_list_directory 48 KB execute_shell_command 32 KB web_search, MCP tools, default 32 KB

Full outputs are stored under TOOL_OUTPUT_DIR, which defaults to a tool-outputs/ directory in the legacy chat scratch directory (<tempdir>/yaicli/chats/tool-outputs) — independent of the per-project session store. The truncated text includes the path so the model can read the rest:

{"file_paths": ["/path/to/tool-outputs/20261104-123456-execute_shell_command.txt"], "offset": 20000, "limit": 12000}

fs_read_file accepts two optional paging arguments (character based, applied per file):

Argument Meaning offset First character to return (0 = beginning of the file). limit Maximum number of characters to return (0 = read to the end).

The response keeps the usual path/success/content/size/error fields and adds offset/limit (the requested window), total_chars (full file length), returned_chars and truncated (whether content is only a window of the file). Paging works on the original file as well as on a spilled tool output; when reading a spilled output, remember it is the JSON text of the tool result, not the original file. fs_read_file results are themselves capped at 64 KB, so pass a limit comfortably below that (e.g. limit: 12000) to avoid the page being truncated again.

Notes:

  • Set TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS=0 to disable truncation (not recommended for agent loops).
  • The terminal preview is a separate, much tighter display-only limit: TOOL_DISPLAY_MAX_LINES=15 lines and TOOL_DISPLAY_MAX_CHARS=4000 characters. Tool results are rendered head-only with a … +N lines · Ctrl+O to expand marker, so a 1 MB shell result does not flood your screen. This never changes what the model receives — the model still gets up to TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS characters; set both display limits to 0 to show everything.
  • Ctrl+O (or /show-output) opens a full-screen viewer with every tool output of the current turn: left pane lists the entries (tool name, size and a command/path caption), right pane shows the selected result. ↑/↓ select, Tab switches pane, PgUp/PgDn scroll, f toggles between the model-visible text and the spilled full file (capped at 1 MB), and q/Esc/Ctrl+O closes it, restoring the REPL. Non-interactive runs fall back to the inline last-output panel.
  • The same shortcut works while the assistant is generating an answer: the viewer opens without waiting for the turn to finish and the generation keeps running in a background worker thread while it is open; closing it redraws the accumulated answer and streaming continues. Typed-ahead text is kept and pre-filled into the next prompt.
  • Long tool-call arguments on the @Function call: line are summarized (TOOL_CALL_PREVIEW_MAX_CHARS=300); a large content/command value appears as <N chars>.
  • If the spill file cannot be written (read-only disk, permission error), YAICLI degrades to plain truncation without the path — the request still succeeds.
  • Spilled files are created with mode 0600 on POSIX (file output may contain secrets); clean the TOOL_OUTPUT_DIR up periodically.

docs.title: 2. Token budget
docs.text:
Three numbers decide how much of the conversation is sent in one request:

Term Meaning Window The model's total context window (input + output) — e.g. 128,000 tokens for gpt-4o, 1,000,000 for Gemini 2.5 Pro. Budget How many input tokens one request may use: min(window, max_input) - MAX_TOKENS - CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS. Reserve Output headroom kept out of the budget: MAX_TOKENS + CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS (default 1024 + 1024 = 2048).

Before each provider request, YAICLI estimates the tokens in the conversation (a stdlib heuristic: ~3.5 characters per token with corrections for CJK text, plus a fixed per-message overhead) and compares it with the budget. If the conversation is over budget, YAICLI first trims mechanically — no extra API call, no extra cost — then sends the request. Trimming by message count alone is not enough: a tool_calls message must never be separated from its tool results, or every provider rejects the payload. YAICLI therefore trims by turn group:

  • a turn group is one user message plus the assistant/tool messages that follow it;
  • whole groups are dropped, oldest first;
  • an assistant message with tool_calls is always kept together with its tool results (zero orphan tool messages);
  • leading system/context messages are preserved;
  • one line is printed to stderr when trimming happens, so you know why old context disappeared.

docs.title: How the window is resolved
docs.text:
yaicli/model_limits.py resolves the window in six short-circuiting layers: the first hit wins, and every result carries a source saying where the number came from.

# source Where the number comes from 1 user MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS (YAI_MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS): an explicit override, always highest priority. 2 learned The real limit parsed from a provider context-length error in a previous request (cached 30 days). 3 metadata Provider-advertised metadata — OpenRouter /models, Gemini models.get, Ollama /api/show (cached 7 days). 4 catalog The bundled snapshot yaicli/data/model_limits.json. 5 heuristic Provider-scoped family prefix, longest match wins (gpt-4-32k is not gpt-4); Ollama falls back to 8,192. 6 default 128,000 tokens for a model nothing else knows, plus a one-time warning.

/context shows the result on the window line: the value, the source, and a short detail when the layer provides one (source: metadata · openrouter /models). source: user means your config won; source: default means the model is unknown (see below).

docs.title: Normalization and matching
docs.text:
Model ids are normalized before the static layers see them: lower-cased; up to two vendor prefixes removed (openrouter/, anthropic/, openai/, google/, mistralai/, meta-llama/, qwen/, deepseek/, moonshotai/, x-ai/, cohere/, nvidia/); a -YYYYMMDD / @YYYYMMDD suffix removed; OpenRouter variant suffixes (:free, :batch, :extended, :nitro, :online) removed; and a [1m] marker stripped (the raw id with [1m] resolves to 1,000,000 as a heuristic hit).

The catalog is matched exactly on the normalized id (it is a curated snapshot, not a fuzzy table); the heuristic layer matches provider-scoped prefixes, longest match first. This ordering is deliberate: an exact catalog entry for grok-4 (256,000) does not silently apply to grok-4.7 — that id falls through to the grok family heuristic (131,072) until a catalog entry, provider metadata or a MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS override exists for it.

Ollama is special-cased: generic cloud families (qwen, mistral, ...) are ignored there because a local server serves those names with its own runtime window, so an unknown local model resolves to OLLAMA_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW (8,192). The provider's NUM_CTX option is not used as a window; only configured values, learned values, provider metadata and the catalog are authoritative.

docs.title: Heuristic family table
docs.text:
Longest prefix wins, so gpt-4-32k beats gpt-4 and o1-mini beats o1. The table lives in HEURISTIC_CONTEXT_WINDOWS in yaicli/model_limits.py; anything that does not match any row falls to the default.

Window Family prefixes 1,048,576 gemini 1,047,576 gpt-4.1 400,000 gpt-5 245,760 minimax 200,000 claude, o1, o3, o4 131,072 moonshot, kimi, qwen, grok 128,000 gpt-4o, gpt-4-turbo, o1-mini, deepseek, glm, chatglm, mistral, command, cohere 32,768 gpt-4-32k, mixtral 16,385 gpt-3.5 8,192 gpt-4 (plain gpt-4; the longer gpt-4* rows win), llama (Ollama only)

docs.title: Overriding the window (MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS)
docs.text:
Set MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS (a JSON object; the YAI_MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS env var works too) to pin a window yourself. Keys may name a bare model (applies to any provider), a provider:model pair, or a provider/model pair; values may be an integer or an object with window / max_input / max_output:

[core]
# JSON: keys may be "model", "provider:model" or "provider/model";
# values may be an int or an object with window / max_input / max_output.
MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS={"my-gateway-model": 200000, "openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5": 1000000, "ollama/qwen2.5:7b": {"window": 32768, "max_output": 4096}}

An explicit entry always wins over everything below it, and /context then reports source: user. Remove the entry to fall back to the learned/metadata/catalog/heuristic layers.

docs.title: Provider metadata probes
docs.text:
When no user or learned value exists, YAICLI asks the provider for the real limit. The probe is lazy (only when the budget is first needed), single-attempt, bounded to 2 seconds, and completely silent on errors or timeouts — it simply falls through to the catalog:

Provider Probe Fields used OpenRouter GET {BASE_URL}/models context_length, top_provider.max_completion_tokens Gemini models.get input_token_limit, output_token_limit Ollama /api/show the largest positive model_info.*.context_length

The result is cached per (provider, base_url, model). Failed or empty probes are also remembered in-process for 5 minutes (METADATA_MISS_TTL_SECONDS=300), so an offline or metadata-less provider pays the ≤2 s timeout on the first request only instead of on every turn. Set ENABLE_MODEL_METADATA=false to skip probes entirely (no extra network calls at all).

docs.title: Learning the real limit from a context-length error
docs.text:
Even with estimation, a provider can reject a request as too long (the exact window differs per model). When the error text carries the real limit (for example maximum context length is 200000 tokens), YAICLI parses it and records it as a learned value — in memory immediately and on disk for the next session (30 days). The request is re-trimmed to the new budget and retried once; the stderr notice names the learned number:

Provider rejected the request as too long; learned the real context limit (200,000 tokens), dropped 1 older message(s) and retrying once (210,000 -> 197,952 est. tokens).

The next /context then reports source: learned, and subsequent requests use the corrected window.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
Resolved windows are cached in <config-dir>/cache/model_limits.json (next to config.ini):

  • provider metadata: 7 days;
  • learned limits: 30 days.

Set ENABLE_MODEL_LIMITS_CACHE=false to keep the cache in memory only — nothing is read from or written to disk. Deleting the file is always safe: it is a pure cache and is rebuilt on demand.

docs.title: Explicit budget override and safety headroom
docs.text: Setting Meaning CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS 0 (default) = derive from the window (window - MAX_TOKENS - CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS). A value > 0 overrides the derived budget verbatim — the legacy behaviour, useful as a hard cap or a fallback. CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS Extra headroom kept below window - MAX_TOKENS for tokenizer/request drift (default 1024). Raise it if you still hit "too long" errors; 0 disables the headroom. MAX_TOKENS The requested output limit. It is reserved from the window but never rewritten by YAICLI.

docs.title: Unknown-model warning
docs.text:
When the resolved source is default and a model is configured, the first request of every session prints a two-line warning to stderr; the numbers are still shown and the message says how to fix them:

Context window for model "my-gateway-model" is unknown; assuming 128,000 tokens (source: default).
Set MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS={"my-gateway-model": 200000} or CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS to override.

docs.title: 3. Context-length self-healing
docs.text:
Even with estimation, a provider can reject a request with a context_length error (the exact window differs per model). When that happens, YAICLI:

  1. parses the real limit from the error text when present (for example maximum context length is 200000 tokens) and records it as a learned value — in memory and in the on-disk cache — so the next request, /context and /compact all use the corrected window;
  2. re-trims the payload to the new budget, dropping whole turn groups;
  3. retries the request once;
  4. if it still fails, prints an actionable error (provider, cause, suggestion) and exits with the usual error code — instead of the previous behaviour of failing every subsequent request.

A single turn that is already too large cannot be trimmed: YAICLI still records the learned limit, then prints the actionable error instead of retrying forever. In the REPL you can also recover manually with /clear or /compact.

docs.title: 4. Inspecting and compacting the conversation
docs.text:
In the interactive REPL:

Command Description /context or /ctx Show the estimated context usage: resolved window and its source, role prompt, project context, /add context, history/tool output, total vs budget, remaining and reserve. Subcommands: list, clear, add <path>, remove <path>, budget. /compact [keep_rounds] Manually compact the conversation, keeping the last N turns (turn groups); older ones are dropped from the outgoing request. Without an argument the default retention applies. /clear Start over with an empty history.

Bare /context prints the usage block and then the legacy /add file list; /context budget (aliases stats / usage) prints only the usage block. The subcommand list is printed only for an unknown subcommand (Available: list, clear, add <path>, remove <path>, budget):

Context usage (estimated):
  window        : 1,000,000 tokens (source: metadata · openrouter /models)
  role prompt   : 12 tokens
  project ctx   : 1,234 tokens
  /add context  : 0 tokens
  history       : 2,175 tokens (tool output 1,148)
  overhead      : 3 tokens
  total         : 3,424 / 997,952 tokens (0.3%)
  remaining     : 994,528 tokens
  reserve       : 2,048 (MAX_TOKENS 1,024 + safety 1,024)
  Use /compact [keep_rounds] to drop older turn groups.
  • window is the resolved model window plus where it came from (source: metadata · openrouter /models above). An unknown model renders source: default · assumed for unknown model; set MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS to override.
  • role prompt, project ctx, /add context and history are the token buckets the next request carries (tool output is the part of history that came from tools).
  • overhead is the fixed request priming tokens (REQUEST_OVERHEAD_TOKENS = 3) that are not part of any message; it is counted in total and shown so the rows add up to the total.
  • total is checked against the request budget; remaining is what is left of it.
  • reserve is the output headroom kept out of the window (MAX_TOKENS + CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS).

Use /context when a session starts behaving as if it forgot earlier steps (check the window source first — an unknown model may be budgeted far below its real window); then /compact to reclaim budget deliberately, pin a window with MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS, or raise CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS to a hard value.

docs.title: 5. Tokens & cost
docs.text:
YAICLI measures what a run actually costs (v0.22 K17). Token counts come from the provider response whenever the provider reports them, so they are exact for the request. When a provider does not report usage (or an OpenAI-compatible proxy rejects the streaming usage option), YAICLI falls back to the same heuristic as the budget estimator and marks the numbers as estimated instead of hiding them.

  • per request: prompt/completion/total tokens, plus prompt-cache hits (cached_tokens) and reasoning tokens (reasoning_tokens) when the provider reports them;
  • per session: totals per model, request count, and tool metrics (call count, total wall-clock duration, result characters the model saw);
  • per run: the last provider finish_reason (so a "length" truncation is visible).

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
Cost is an estimate in USD, computed as tokens / 1M × price per model. The built-in price table covers common OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen and GLM models (approximate public list prices). Override it for exact accounting — and to price models the table does not know — with MODEL_PRICING, a JSON object of model-prefix to USD-per-1M-token prices:

[core]
# JSON; prefixes are matched longest-first, and override the built-in table
MODEL_PRICING={"gpt-4o": {"input": 2.5, "output": 10}, "my-local-model": {"input": 0, "output": 0}}

Unknown models are reported as "unknown model pricing" (and cost_usd: null in JSON output) instead of a guessed number. With cache pricing the estimate is intentionally conservative: cached tokens are still billed at the full input price.

docs.title: Showing usage
docs.text:
Where What SHOW_USAGE (default true) One dim line after each interactive turn, e.g. tokens 1,234 in / 567 out · $0.0021 · 1.2s · stop. Unknown cost is simply omitted; machine/headless output never prints it. /cost (interactive) Session totals, per-model breakdown, estimated USD cost, tool call metrics and the last finish reason. --output-format json The full usage object + finish_reason (see Headless & Scripting). --output-format stream-json A final usage event with the same numbers.

When finish_reason is "length" the answer was truncated by the output token limit: YAICLI prints one MAX_TOKENS warning to stderr in every mode and reports finish_reason: "length" in structured output. Raise MAX_TOKENS (or reduce the context/tool output sent) to get complete answers.

docs.title: 6. Session and memory limits
docs.text:
• INTERACTIVE_ROUND (default 25) is the number of chat turns kept in the REPL (×2 messages), not a token limit. Token trimming is described above.
  • MAX_HISTORY (default 500) is the number of entries in the prompt history file — it has no effect on the conversation context.
  • Tool outputs already spilled to TOOL_OUTPUT_DIR are not re-sent automatically; they only enter the context if the model reads them back.
  • Image input is bounded by the provider; keep images reasonably small (the local cache also holds the base64 payload in the session).

docs.title: Recommended settings for long tasks
docs.text:
[core]
# Budget: 0 = derive from the resolved window (window - MAX_TOKENS - safety);
# a value > 0 overrides it verbatim as a hard cap.
CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS=0
# Extra headroom below window - MAX_TOKENS; raise it if you still hit "too long" errors.
CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS=1024
# Pin a window when the provider/catalog does not report the model correctly.
# MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS={"my-gateway-model": 200000}
# Lower to reduce tokens per tool result if your model has a small window
TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS=16000
# More tool rounds before the depth limit stops the run
MAX_TOOL_CALL_DEPTH=12

docs.title: Related configuration
docs.text: Key Default Purpose TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS 32000 Per-tool-result character cap (0 = unlimited) TOOL_OUTPUT_DIR <tempdir>/yaicli/chats/tool-outputs Where full tool outputs are spilled (independent of the per-project session store) TOOL_DISPLAY_MAX_LINES 15 Terminal preview lines (0 = unlimited; model unaffected) TOOL_DISPLAY_MAX_CHARS 4000 Terminal preview characters (0 = unlimited; model unaffected) TOOL_CALL_PREVIEW_MAX_CHARS 300 Max characters of the @Function call: argument line (0 = raw) CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS 0 (derive from window) Per-request token budget (> 0 = verbatim override) MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS - (empty map) JSON per-model context-window overrides (model / provider:model / provider/model keys) ENABLE_MODEL_METADATA true Probe provider metadata (OpenRouter / Gemini / Ollama) for the model window CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS 1024 Extra headroom below window - MAX_TOKENS when deriving the budget ENABLE_MODEL_LIMITS_CACHE true Cache resolved windows in <config-dir>/cache/model_limits.json (7-day metadata / 30-day learned TTLs) MAX_TOOL_CALL_DEPTH 8 Tool rounds per request (--max-turns overrides per run) EXIT_ON_DEPTH_LIMIT true One-shot run exits non-zero when the tool-round limit is reached INTERACTIVE_ROUND 25 Chat turns kept in the REPL SHOW_USAGE true Print one dim token/cost line after each interactive turn MODEL_PRICING {} JSON price overrides ({"model-prefix": {"input": x, "output": y}}, USD per 1M tokens)

docs.title: File Context Management
docs.text: YAICLI provides powerful file context management capabilities that allow you to include files and directories in your AI conversations. This helps the AI understand your codebase, configuration files, documentation, and any other relevant context.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
There are two ways to include files in your conversations:

  1. Persistent Context (/add): Add files/directories that stay in context for the entire session
  2. Temporary References (@): Reference files on-the-fly for a single message

docs.title: Persistent Context
docs.text: Use the /add command to add files or directories to your session context. These items remain available throughout your conversation until you remove them.

docs.title: Adding Files
docs.text:
# Add a single file
/add src/main.py
# Output: Added file to context: /path/to/src/main.py

# Add a directory (scans recursively)
/add tests/
# Output: Added directory to context: /path/to/tests/

# Add several files: /add takes one path per command
/add config.yaml
/add README.md

/add reads a single path per invocation (extra arguments are ignored); repeat the command for each file.

docs.title: Removing Context Items
docs.text:
# Remove by exact path
/context remove /path/to/src/main.py

# Remove by filename (partial match)
/context remove main.py

# Clear all context
/context clear

docs.title: Complete Command Reference
docs.text: Command Alias Description /add <path> - Add file/directory to context /context list /ctx list List all context items /context clear /ctx clear Remove all items /context add <path> - Same as /add /context remove <path> /ctx rm Remove specific item

docs.title: Temporary @ References
docs.text: For quick, one-time file inclusion, use the @ symbol directly in your messages.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
# Reference a single file
@README.md What is this project about?

# Reference multiple files
@src/main.py @config.yaml Explain the architecture

# The AI sees the file contents and responds based on them

docs.title: Paths with Spaces
docs.text:
Use quotes for filenames or paths containing spaces:

@"my document.txt" Summarize this

@'path with spaces/file.md' What does this do?

docs.title: Auto-completion
docs.text:
Type @ and press Tab to browse files:

💬 > @src/[Tab]
# Shows file browser:
# src/main.py
# src/utils.py
# src/config/

Use arrow keys to navigate and select files.

docs.title: File Reading Process
docs.text:
1. File Detection: YAICLI checks if the path exists
  2. Type Check: Determines if it's a file or directory
  3. Content Reading:
  4. Files: Read entire content
  5. Directories: Recursively scan (2 levels deep by default)
  6. Formatting: Content is formatted as Markdown code blocks
  7. Submission: Formatted content is sent to the AI as a system message

docs.title: Smart File Handling
docs.text:
Binary Files: Automatically skipped - Images: .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .ico - Archives: .zip, .tar, .gz - Compiled: .pyc, .pdf

Size Limits: Files larger than 1MB are skipped

Encoding: UTF-8 with error replacement for non-UTF-8 characters

docs.title: Directory Scanning
docs.text:
When you add a directory, YAICLI:

  1. Scans files recursively (default: 2 levels deep)
  2. Skips hidden files (starting with .)
  3. Ignores common patterns:
  4. .git/
  5. __pycache__/
  6. .venv/, venv/
  7. node_modules/
  8. .idea/, .vscode/
  9. .DS_Store

Example Directory Structure:

project/
├── src/
│   ├── main.py
│   └── utils/
│       ├── helpers.py
│       └── config.py
├── tests/
│   └── test_main.py
└── .git/          # Skipped
└── node_modules/  # Skipped

/add src/
# Includes:
# - src/main.py
# - src/utils/helpers.py
# - src/utils/config.py

docs.title: Codebase Analysis
docs.text:
# Add entire source directory
/add src/

💬 > Explain the architecture of this codebase
# AI now has full visibility into src/

docs.title: Configuration Review
docs.text:
# Multiple config files
/add .env
/add docker-compose.yml
/add config.yaml

💬 > Are there any security issues in this configuration?
# AI reviews all config files together

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
# Add error log and source file
/add error.log
/add src/handler.py

💬 > Why is this error happening in handler.py?
# AI correlates the error with source code

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
# Quick reference for documentation
@api-docs.md @docs/api-guide.md Implement this endpoint

# vs persistent context for long sessions
/add docs/

💬 > Help me implement user authentication
💬 > Now add password reset
💬 > Finally, add email verification
# docs/ stays in context for entire session

docs.title: When to Use /add (Persistent)
docs.text:
• Working on a specific feature: Add relevant source files
  • Code reviews: Include all files being reviewed
  • Debugging sessions: Keep error logs and source files available
  • Documentation: Reference docs while implementing features
  • Multi-step tasks: Avoid repeating file references

docs.title: When to Use @ (Temporary)
docs.text:
• Quick questions: One-time file checks
  • Comparing files: @file1.json @file2.json
  • Minimal context: Don't clutter the conversation
  • Ad-hoc analysis: Quick look at a file

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
1. Be Specific: Add only relevant files to avoid context bloat
  2. Clean Up: Remove items with /context remove when done
  3. Check Context: Use /context list to see what's active
  4. Use Quoted Paths: For files with spaces, use @"path"
  5. Combine Both: Use /add for core files, @ for temporary references

docs.title: Example Workflow
docs.text:
# Start a coding session
ai --chat

# Add core source files
/add src/
/add config.yaml

💬 > Add a new user registration endpoint

# Add a specific test file temporarily
@tests/test_auth.py Write tests for this

# Reference documentation once
@docs/api-spec.md Follow these specs

# Context still has src/ and config.yaml
💬 > Update the password validation

# Clean up when done
/context clear

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• File Size: Files > 1MB are skipped
  • Binary Files: Automatically filtered out
  • Directory Depth: Limited to 2 levels by default
  • Context Window: Total content limited by your model's context window
  • Session Scope: Context doesn't persist across different ai invocations

docs.title: File Not Found
docs.text:
💬 > /add nonexistent.py
Error: Path does not exist: /path/to/nonexistent.py

Solution: Use relative paths from current directory or absolute paths

docs.title: Image References
docs.text:
💬 > @diagram.png What does this show?

Expected behavior: image files (.jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .webp) referenced with @ are attached as image input for vision-capable providers; no "binary file" warning is produced. On providers without vision support the CLI warns that the image will be ignored.

docs.title: Binary File Warning
docs.text:
💬 > @document.pdf Summarize this
Warning: Cannot include @document.pdf: [Binary file omitted]

Expected behavior: non-image binary files (.pdf, .zip, compiled files, ...) are skipped; convert them to text (or use a different tool) first.

docs.title: Too Large Warning
docs.text:
💬 > @large-file.log
Warning: Cannot include @large-file.log: [File too large: 2097152 bytes - omitted]

Solution: Split the file or extract relevant portions

docs.title: Context Too Long
docs.text:
If the AI stops responding or behaves unexpectedly, the request may be over the token budget. YAICLI trims old conversation turns automatically and retries once when a provider rejects the request as too long; if it still fails it prints an actionable error.

Solution: 

/context            # show estimated token usage and remaining budget
/compact 5          # keep only the 5 most recent turns
/context list       # remove unnecessary context files
/context remove <path>

See Context & Limits for truncation, the token budget and self-healing.

docs.title: Related Features
docs.text:
• Project Context: .yaicli.md / AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md are auto-loaded from the repository — see Project Context
  • Function Calling: Use functions to interact with the file system
  • Pipe Input: cat file.txt | ai "analyze this"
  • MCP Tools: External tools for file system operations
  • History Management: Save and restore conversations with context

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Command Reference
  • Interactive Mode
  • Configuration

docs.title: Headless & Scripting
docs.text:
YAICLI is designed to be scriptable: a one-shot run can be piped, redirected, parsed by jq, and its exit code can be trusted by CI. This page documents that contract.

The rule is simple:

  • stdout carries the result only (in text, json or stream-json form);
  • stderr carries everything else — labels, tool previews, warnings, errors, retry/trim notices;
  • the exit code describes the outcome.

docs.title: Quick examples
docs.text:
# One explicit one-shot run
ai -p "What is the capital of France?"

# Answer only, safe for shell substitution
summary=$(ai -q -p "Summarize README.md in one sentence")

# Machine-readable result
ai -p "List the files changed in the last commit" --output-format json | jq -r .content
# --json is a shorthand for --output-format json
ai -p "Summarize this repository" --json | jq -r .content

# Streaming events (one JSON object per line)
ai -p "Find and fix the failing test" --output-format stream-json | jq -c 'select(.type=="tool_call")'

# Pipe input into the agent
cat error.log | ai -p "Explain these errors and suggest a fix"

# CI: allow the shell tool for this run and fail the step when a tool is denied
ai -p "Run the test suite and summarize failures" \
  --allowed-tools "execute_shell_command" -y --fail-on-tool-denied

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Method Example Behaviour Prompt argument ai "explain this repo" One-shot with the given prompt Stdin echo hi \| ai Stdin content becomes the prompt Both cat app.py \| ai "review this" Stdin content is prepended to the prompt argument -p/--print ai -p "..." Explicit one-shot mode; never starts the REPL
  • When stdin is not a TTY, --chat is ignored (a warning is printed to stderr) because a REPL cannot read from a pipe.
  • -p/--print is the explicit form of a one-shot run. Use it in scripts for clarity: it forces the headless contract (plain output, no prompts/REPL) even on a terminal. --output-format other than text and -q also imply one-shot; --chat is then ignored with a stderr warning.
  • The REPL is only started by --chat (or by an interactive ai with no prompt).

docs.title: --output-format text (default)
docs.text: Human-readable text. In a non-TTY (pipe/redirect) this is plain text: no banner, no Rich Live animation, no ANSI/box drawing. The output ends with exactly one newline.

docs.title: --output-format json
docs.text:
One JSON object on stdout. All diagnostics go to stderr.

{
  "content": "The final assistant answer as markdown text.",
  "tool_calls": [
    {"name": "fs_read_file", "arguments": {"file_paths": ["README.md"]}, "result": "..."}
  ],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 1234,
    "completion_tokens": 456,
    "total_tokens": 1690,
    "cached_tokens": 0,
    "reasoning_tokens": 0,
    "estimated": false,
    "requests": 1,
    "cost_usd": 0.0077,
    "models": {
      "gpt-4o-mini": {
        "prompt_tokens": 1234,
        "completion_tokens": 456,
        "total_tokens": 1690,
        "estimated": false,
        "cost_usd": 0.0077
      }
    },
    "tools": {"count": 1, "duration_ms": 42.0, "result_chars": 1024}
  },
  "finish_reason": "stop",
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "provider": "openai",
  "error": null,
  "exit_code": 0
}
Field Meaning content Final assistant answer text tool_calls Ordered list of tool calls made during the run usage Real token usage and cost for the run (see below) finish_reason Last provider finish_reason ("stop", "length", "tool_calls", "depth_limit", or null when unknown) model, provider Effective model/provider for this run error Exactly null on success, otherwise {"kind": "<error kind>", "message": "<detail>"}. Possible kinds: auth, rate_limit, context_length, network, timeout, bad_request, provider, tool, config, depth_limit, interrupted, unknown exit_code Exit code the process will return (see below)

usage is no longer zeroed (v0.22 K17):

usage key Meaning prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens Provider-reported token counts. prompt_tokens/completion_tokens are kept at the top level for backwards compatibility. cached_tokens Prompt-cache hits (provider-dependent; 0 when not reported) reasoning_tokens Reasoning/thinking tokens included in completion_tokens (provider-dependent) estimated true when the provider reported no usage and the numbers are a heuristic estimate (see Context & Limits) requests Number of provider requests made during the run (tool rounds included) cost_usd Estimated cost in USD from the built-in price table, overridden by MODEL_PRICING. null when no price is known for the model. models Per-model breakdown (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, estimated, cost_usd) tools Executed tool calls: count, duration_ms (wall clock) and result_chars (size of the results the model saw)

When the model stops because the output token limit was reached, finish_reason is "length" and one Response stopped at MAX_TOKENS; ... warning is printed to stderr in every output mode (stdout stays clean/parseable). Increase MAX_TOKENS (or shrink the prompt/tool output) to get a complete answer.

One limitation: failures that happen before a result exists (for example an invalid provider configuration, a missing API key during client creation, or a usage error such as exit 2) print a diagnostic to stderr and exit non-zero without emitting the JSON object; every run that reaches a result emits exactly one object. An interrupted one-shot run is reported both ways: exit 130 and, if JSON output was active, error.kind = "interrupted".

docs.title: --output-format stream-json
docs.text:
Newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON): one event object per line, in order. This is the format to use for progress UIs, cancellation and tool-trace collection.

Event When Fields turn_start A model request starts type, turn (0-based round index) text_delta The model streams answer text type, delta (new text since the previous chunk) tool_call The model requests a tool type, name, arguments (parsed JSON when possible) tool_result A tool has finished type, name, result (the tool result text as seen by the model, truncated as in context) usage The run finished collecting usage type, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, cached_tokens, reasoning_tokens, estimated, requests, cost_usd, models, tools, and finish_reason when known (same values as the JSON usage object) done The run finished type, exit_code, error (null or {kind, message})

Events are flushed per line. text_delta events stream during generation; tool_call / tool_result pairs are emitted at round boundaries (after the tools have executed), and usage / done are emitted at the end. Every event object has a type field; unknown event types must be ignored by consumers so that new event kinds can be added without breaking scripts. Example:

{"type": "turn_start", "turn": 0}
{"type": "text_delta", "delta": "I will check the "}
{"type": "tool_call", "name": "fs_read_file", "arguments": {"file_paths": ["README.md"]}}
{"type": "tool_result", "name": "fs_read_file", "result": "# YAICLI ..."}
{"type": "usage", "prompt_tokens": 1234, "completion_tokens": 456, "total_tokens": 1690, "cached_tokens": 0, "reasoning_tokens": 0, "estimated": false, "requests": 1, "cost_usd": 0.0077, "models": {"gpt-4o-mini": {"prompt_tokens": 1234, "completion_tokens": 456, "total_tokens": 1690, "estimated": false, "cost_usd": 0.0077}}, "tools": {"count": 1, "duration_ms": 42.0, "result_chars": 1024}, "finish_reason": "stop"}
{"type": "done", "exit_code": 0, "error": null}

docs.title: -q/--quiet
docs.text: Only the answer on stdout: no labels, no tool preview boxes, no progress. Errors still go to stderr. Combine with -p and either text or JSON output.

docs.title: Streaming and the terminal
docs.text:
Streaming stays on by default in a TTY. With a pipe or a redirect, YAICLI disables the Live region and cursor animation and prints the result plainly, so ai ... > file.md produces a clean file. Without -p, -q or a non-text output format, a TTY keeps the normal rich experience (labels and panels); the machine contract applies as soon as output is piped.

Use --no-stream if you want a single final block instead of streamed chunks.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Success: an answer was produced (also informational commands such as --version / --list-*) 1 Handled failure: invalid config/provider, auth/API error, network failure, no input, unexpected error 2 Usage error: invalid option or argument (including an unknown --output-format value or an invalid --cwd) 3 A tool was denied and --fail-on-tool-denied was set 130 Interrupted by SIGINT (Ctrl+C) during a one-shot run or generation 141 Broken pipe (EPIPE): the producer side of a pipeline such as ai --help \| head -1. If the write wins the race, the same command may exit 0; it never exits 1 for a closed pipe.

Inside the interactive REPL, an error during one turn is printed and the session continues; leaving the REPL normally exits 0. Use one-shot (-p / prompt argument) when the exit code must reflect the request outcome.

docs.title: SIGINT (Ctrl+C)
docs.text:
• One-shot runs (including while the answer is generating): interrupts, prints one short line to stderr and exits 130 — no traceback.
  • REPL prompt: a single Ctrl+C clears the current input and stays in the REPL; pressing it a second time within ~2 seconds exits normally.
  • REPL generation: cancels the turn and returns to the prompt (a second Ctrl+C at the prompt exits).
  • Ctrl+D at the REPL prompt exits normally with 0.

docs.title: EPIPE (| head, closed pipes)
docs.text: Writing to a closed pipe never produces a traceback or a spurious non-zero error message: ai --help | head -1 is safe and exits 0/141. The same applies to long streamed answers piped into tools that stop reading early.

docs.title: Non-interactive approvals
docs.text:
In a pipe/CI there is no terminal to ask, so unapproved tool calls are denied by default. Three flags control this:

Flag Effect -y/--yes Auto-approve read-level tools only (read risk class). Write, network and exec tools are still denied unless separately allowed. With --shell in a non-TTY it is also the explicit switch that lets the generated command execute. --allowed-tools "a,b*" Per-run allowlist. Comma-separated tool names or glob patterns (fs_*, execute_shell_command). This is the explicit way to pre-approve write/exec tools. --fail-on-tool-denied Exit with code 3 if any tool call was denied (otherwise the model just receives the refusal and continues).

Persistent rules live in tool_permissions.json and are documented in Permissions & Safety. Danger-classified shell commands are always refused non-interactively, even when the tool itself is allowed.

TOOL_CONFIRM=false is still supported for fully unattended runs, but it grants every tool call without a prompt (apart from danger classification). Prefer --allowed-tools when you only need a few tools.

docs.title: Run limits
docs.text: Option Effect --max-turns N Maximum number of tool-call rounds for this run (N >= 1; maps to MAX_TOOL_CALL_DEPTH, default 8). When the limit is reached, the run stops with a depth_limit result; with EXIT_ON_DEPTH_LIMIT=true (default) a one-shot run exits non-zero. --cwd DIR Working directory for the run; also becomes WORKSPACE_ROOT for the shell cwd and the guarded file writes. Paths outside the workspace are rejected (see Workspace Safety). --output-format ..., -q, -p Output contract, described above.

docs.title: Non-interactive --shell
docs.text: --shell is an interactive convenience by default (it shows the generated command and asks before executing). When stdin/stdout is not a TTY, ai --shell "..." prints the generated command to stdout and does not execute it, exiting 0. Add -y/--yes to execute it in a trusted context; if the command itself then exits non-zero, the run exits 1.

docs.title: CI recipe
docs.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# 1. The agent may read files and run the test command without prompting.
# 2. Any denied tool fails the job instead of silently degrading.
ai -p "Read the failing tests, find the root cause and write a short report to CI_REPORT.md" \
  --output-format json \
  --allowed-tools "fs_*,execute_shell_command" \
  --max-turns 12 \
  --cwd "$PWD" \
  --fail-on-tool-denied > result.json

jq -e '.exit_code == 0' result.json
jq -r '.content' result.json

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• No output at all: errors go to stderr. Re-run and capture both: ai -p "..." >out.txt 2>err.txt.
  • jq: parse error: make sure you used -p/a prompt and --output-format json; text is the default. Warnings always go to stderr, so stdout remains parseable.
  • Tool denied in CI: add --allowed-tools for the tools the task needs; --yes alone only covers read-level tools.
  • Exit code 130 in CI: the job sent SIGINT (timeout/cancel) — check the CI timeout settings.
  • Long tasks stop early: raise --max-turns; the run reports a depth-limit message on stderr.
  • Answers are cut off mid-sentence: finish_reason is "length" and a MAX_TOKENS warning is printed to stderr — raise MAX_TOKENS (or lower the amount of context/tool output sent).

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text:
The prompt is a single fixed line: the mode icon plus >. Nothing else is inlined, so the cursor always starts in the same column regardless of the model, role or working directory.

 💬 >
  • The model, the last-known context usage and the per-turn token/cost figures are shown on the dim status line that closes each answer, for example gpt-4o · context 12% · tokens 1,234 in / 567 out · $0.0021 · 1.2s · stop. The current model is also printed in the welcome banner (Model: gpt-4o) and /model changes it immediately.
  • The working directory, git branch and assistant role are not shown. In particular, a custom DEFAULT_ROLE (for example master) is ordinary assistant configuration, not repository state: the prompt never inspects the repository.
  • A Shift+Tab mode switch changes the input-line icon (💬 chat, 🚀 execute, 📝 temporary session).
  • The status line is interactive-only and obeys SHOW_USAGE; headless/one-shot runs never render it, and the context percentage stays cached (refreshed after every completed turn and after /compact, /clear, /load and /model).

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• /help|? - Show help message
  • /clear - Clear conversation history
  • /his - Show chat history
  • /list - List saved chats
  • /save <title> - Save current chat with title
  • /load <index> - Load a saved chat
  • /del <index> - Delete a saved chat
  • /add <path> - Add a file or directory to the persistent context
  • /context or /ctx - Show context/token usage, or manage file context (list, add, remove, clear)
  • /cost - Show session token usage, estimated cost, per-model breakdown and tool metrics
  • /compact [keep_rounds] - Compact the conversation, keeping the last N turns
  • /model - Show the current model and provider
  • /model <name> - Switch the model for this session: the provider client is rebuilt on the next request, the chat history is kept, and the change is not written to the config file. The notice names the previous model so you can revert with /model <old-name>.
  • /role - Show the current role and the available roles
  • /role <name> - Switch the assistant role for this session (case-insensitive; an unknown name lists the available roles). The change is session-only; restart to use the configured role.
  • /retry - Re-run the last user turn from its pre-turn snapshot. Useful after an API error: the failed turn's partial messages are discarded before the same input is sent again.
  • /permissions - List (and revoke) persistent tool approval rules
  • /show-output - Open the full-screen tool-output viewer for this turn
  • /undo - Restore the last file change made by a tool in this session
  • !<command> - Execute a shell command directly
  • /exit - Exit the application
  • /mode chat|exec - Switch modes

Typing / opens the slash-command completion menu: every command is listed with a one-line description, /co filters the list, and Tab/arrow keys select an entry. @ path completion still works as before and shares the same prompt.

docs.title: Usage & cost
docs.text:
Each turn closes with one dim status line: the current model and context usage, then what the turn cost (v0.22 K17), for example:

gpt-4o · context 12% · tokens 1,234 in / 567 out · $0.0021 · 1.2s · stop

The numbers come from the provider when it reports them; a provider that reports no usage gets a clearly estimated count instead. Unknown model pricing simply omits the $ segment. The line is controlled by SHOW_USAGE (default true) and only appears in interactive output — headless / JSON runs report usage through their structured output instead.

  • /cost prints the session totals (tokens in/out, requests, estimated flag), a per-model breakdown, the estimated USD cost, tool-call count/duration/result size and the last finish reason. It works even when the model has no known price ("unknown model pricing").
  • When the model hits the output token limit, the answer is truncated at finish_reason="length"; YAICLI prints one Response stopped at MAX_TOKENS; ... warning to stderr — raise MAX_TOKENS to get complete answers.
  • Prices are approximate built-in estimates (USD per 1M tokens); override them with MODEL_PRICING for exact accounting. See Context & Limits.

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text:
• Shift+Tab - Toggle between Chat/Execute modes
  • Ctrl+C - Clear the current input line; during generation it cancels the turn. Press Ctrl+C twice quickly to exit (single press keeps the session alive)
  • Ctrl+D - Exit (exit code 0)
  • Ctrl+R - Search history
  • Ctrl+O - Open the full-screen tool-output viewer for this turn (↑/↓ select, Tab switch pane, f full text, q/Esc close). It also works while the assistant is generating: generation continues in the background and closing the viewer redraws the accumulated answer
  • ↑/↓ - Navigate through history
  • Alt+Enter (or Esc then Enter) - Insert a newline instead of submitting
  • Ctrl+J - Insert a newline (same as Alt+Enter); Enter still submits the whole input
  • / - Open the slash-command completion menu (see Commands)

Multiline text is useful for pasting or composing long prompts; press Enter once you are done to send the whole buffer as one turn.

docs.title: Chat Mode (💬)
docs.text:
In Chat Mode, you can have natural conversations with the AI while maintaining context: - Full conversation history is maintained - Markdown and code formatting is supported - Reasoning display for complex queries is available

docs.title: Execute Mode (🚀)
docs.text:
Execute Mode allows you to generate shell commands from natural language descriptions: - Generate shell commands from descriptions - Review commands before execution - Edit commands before running - Safe execution with confirmation

 🚀 > Find all PDF files in my Downloads folder
Assistant:
find ~/Downloads -type f -name "*.pdf"
╭─ Suggest Command ──────────────────────╮
│ find ~/Downloads -type f -name "*.pdf" │
╰────────────────────────────────────────╯
Execute command? [e]dit, [y]es, [n]o (y):
Executing...
/Users/username/Downloads/document1.pdf
/Users/username/Downloads/report.pdf
...
